principle: Hashrate is algorithm-specific; do not compare rates across algorithms.

profiles.notes: Bitcoin SHA-256d is not a practical GTX 1650 Ti GPU workload. ASIC or low-difficulty ESP32 NerdMiner only; solo lottery probability is extremely low.
NEXUS generates Stratum settings; ESP32 device performs hashing independently. Does not start the device over USB.
RandomX is CPU-focused; NEXUS must not offer it as GTX 1650 Ti GPU mining.

cpu.status: target requested; RandomX H/s must be measured locally

gpu.status: target_requested; GTX 1650 4GB performance must be measured locally

known_limits: The SHA-256d CPU research benchmark is not a pool miner and does not prove RandomX performance.
SHA-512 digest throughput is not a mining rate.
5 TH/s GPU cannot be treated as a generic target; SHA-256d rates at this scale are ASIC-class, not a consumer GPU expectation.
No hashrate target is accepted without device model, algorithm, stable runtime, accepted/rejected shares, pool-side hashrate and power measurement.
Bitcoin SHA-256d pool configuration does not make a consumer GPU competitive; use ASIC or NerdMiner ESP32.
NerdMiner is an external ESP32 device: NEXUS can generate and validate Stratum configuration but cannot launch its firmware as a Windows process.
RandomX is CPU-only in the NEXUS device selector.
